title: Differential graded compatibility of the module projective model
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, and equip the category $\operatorname{Ch}(\operatorname{Mod}_R)$ of all unbounded cochain complexes with the projective model structure of [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model]. Use the cochain conventions of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. With the usual product-total complex of $R$-linear maps, regarded as a complex of abelian groups, this category is enriched, tensored and cotensored over $\operatorname{Ch}(\operatorname{Ab})$. For an abelian-group complex $T$ and $R$-module complexes $A,B$, the tensor is the direct-sum total $T\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A$, with $R$ acting on $A$, and the cotensor $B^T$ is the product-total $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathbf Z}(T,B)$ with its induced $R$-action. They satisfy the natural complex adjunctions
$$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_R(T\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A,B)\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathbf Z}(T,\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_R(A,B))\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_R(A,B^T).$$
For every cofibration $i:A\to B$ and fibration $p:X\to Y$, the comparison
$$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_R(B,X)\longrightarrow\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_R(A,X)\times_{\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_R(A,Y)}\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_R(B,Y)$$
is degreewise surjective, with kernel naturally isomorphic to $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_R(\operatorname{coker}i,\ker p)$. It is a quasi-isomorphism whenever $i$ or $p$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Thus this is a combinatorial differential graded model category over abelian-group complexes, with exactly the model compatibility axiom specified in [lem-coef-quillen-section-rectification]; no bound on the complexes and no projectivity hypothesis on $R$ as an abelian group is required.

proof.text: Use the unbounded model and cochain conventions of [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model] and [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $H_R(A,B)^n=\prod_{q\in\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Hom}_R(A^q,B^{q+n})$ and $\delta f=d_Bf-(-1)^nf d_A$. Regard these as abelian groups. Expanding gives $\delta^2f=0$ and $\delta(gf)=(\delta g)f+(-1)^{|g|}g\delta f$. Composition is therefore a chain map over $\mathbf Z$; its associativity and unit identities hold componentwise. The identity is a degree-zero cycle, and degree-zero cycles are precisely the cochain maps. This constructs the enrichment. These identities involve two adjacent components only; the product is over all integers.

For $T\in\operatorname{Ch}(\operatorname{Ab})$ put $(T\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A)^k=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}T^p\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A^q$, with $d(t\otimes a)=dt\otimes a+(-1)^pt\otimes da$ and $r(t\otimes a)=t\otimes ra$. Put $(B^T)^k=\prod_p\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(T^p,B^{p+k})$, with $d b=d_Bb-(-1)^kb d_T$ and $(rb)(t)=r b(t)$. The two cross terms cancel in $d^2$ for the tensor; the Hom calculation is Step 1 over $\mathbf Z$. Both differentials are $R$-linear. Direct sums and products of these module groups exist in every degree. The tensor associator sends $(t\otimes u)\otimes a$ to $t\otimes(u\otimes a)$ and its unit is $\mathbf Z[0]$; the differential on either association has the three terms with signs $1,(-1)^{|t|},(-1)^{|t|+|u|}$. The unit and associativity diagrams are thus the identities on pure tensors.

source.place: Tag 0GWN (section-symmetric-monoidal), Tag 0A8H (section-hom-complexes); mixed-coefficient construction written out

proof.text:
The first adjunction sends a homogeneous degree-$n$ map $f:T\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A\to B$ to $g(t)(a)=f(t\otimes a)$. For $|t|=p$, its differential evaluated on $t,a$ is
$$d_B f(t,a)-(-1)^{n+p}f(t,da)-(-1)^n f(dt,a),$$
which is also the curry of $\delta f$. The map is bijective in each degree by the defining bilinear universal property of each tensor summand: a map from a direct sum is a family, and a map into a product is a family. The second adjunction sends the same $f$ to $h(a)(t)=(-1)^{pq}f(t,a)$ for $|a|=q$. Indeed $(\delta h)(a)(t)$ equals
$$(-1)^{pq}d_Bf(t,a)-(-1)^{pq+n}f(dt,a)-(-1)^{pq+n+p}f(t,da),$$
which is $(-1)^{pq}(\delta f)(t,a)$. Its inverse has the same sign. All maps are $R$-linear in $a$, and natural under degree-zero cochain maps in all variables. Evaluating these formulas on homogeneous elements verifies the enriched evaluation and curry identities; composing a curry and its inverse gives the identity with the two signs cancelling. Thus these are complex adjunctions, and their degree-zero cycles give the tensor and cotensor adjunctions for the enrichment of Step 1.

source.place: Tag 0A5Y (lemma-compose), Tag 0GWN (section-symmetric-monoidal); mixed-coefficient currying and both differential identities

proof.text: Let $i:A\to B$ and $p:X\to Y$ be as in the statement, and denote the target pullback complex by $E$. The map $c:H_R(B,X)\to E$ is $w\mapsto(wi,pw)$. Pre- and postcomposition by cochain maps commute with $\delta$, so $c$ is a cochain map. Put $P=\operatorname{coker}i$ and $K=\ker p$, with their induced cochain differentials. A homogeneous map $w$ lies in $\ker c$ exactly when it vanishes on $A$ and has image in $K$. The quotient universal property gives a unique homogeneous $P\to K$, in both directions. Since the quotient and inclusion commute with differentials, this identifies the kernel with $H_R(P,K)$ as a complex. The identification uses no splitting and is natural in $i,p$.

source.place: Tag 0A8H (section-hom-complexes); kernel identification by the module quotient and kernel universal properties

proof.text: By [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model], $i$ splits in each degree, $P$ is dg-projective with projective terms, and $p$ is surjective in each degree. Choose graded maps $r:B\to A$ and $s:P\to B$, and let $q:B\to P$ be the quotient, so $ri=1$, $qs=1$, $ir+sq=1$, $rs=0$. A degree-$n$ element of $E$ is a pair $(u,v)$ with $pu=vi$. For every $q_0\in\mathbf Z$, lift $v s:P^{q_0}\to Y^{q_0+n}$ along $p:X^{q_0+n}\to Y^{q_0+n}$, using the lifting characterization in [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. These choices give a graded degree-$n$ map $\ell:P\to X$. Set $w=ur+\ell q$. Then $wi=u$ and $pw=vi r+v s q=v$. Hence $c$ is degreewise surjective, with no chain-map condition imposed on this homogeneous lift. We now have a degreewise short exact sequence $0\to H_R(P,K)\to H_R(B,X)\xrightarrow c E\to0$.

source.place: Tag 0A8H (section-hom-complexes); degreewise lifting from projective cokernel terms; projectivity as Stacks Tag 05CF in the cited definition

proof.text: If $p$ is a quasi-isomorphism, apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] to $0\to K\to X\xrightarrow pY\to0$. Exactness and the isomorphisms $H^n(p)$ force $H^n(K)=0$ for every integer $n$. The dg-projective property of $P$ in [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model] then gives that $H_R(P,K)$ is acyclic. This uses the acyclicity of the entire product-total Hom, not exactness of a truncated or bounded totalization.

source.place: Tag 0117 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain); apply the dg-projective condition in the cited model statement

proof.text: If $i$ is a quasi-isomorphism, apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] to $0\to A\xrightarrow iB\to P\to0$. The isomorphisms $H^n(i)$ and exactness give $H^n(P)=0$ for all $n$. Since $P$ is dg-projective by [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model], $H_R(P,P)$ is acyclic. Its degree-zero cycle $1_P$ is therefore $\delta h$ for a degree-$(-1)$ map $h:P\to P$, so $d_Ph+hd_P=1_P$. For homogeneous $f\in H_R(P,K)^n$ define $S(f)=(-1)^nfh$. The Leibniz identity of Step 1 gives $\delta S(f)+S(\delta f)=f$. Thus $H_R(P,K)$ is contractible and in particular acyclic for arbitrary $K$. This is a direct consequence of the stated dg-projective condition; it does not require $K$ to be acyclic.

source.place: Tag 0117 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain); explicit contraction obtained from the dg-projective condition and the Hom differential

proof.text: In either case Steps 6 or 7 give an acyclic kernel for the degreewise short exact sequence of Step 5. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] in the abelian category of abelian groups to this sequence: the groups on either side of $H^n(c)$ in the long exact sequence are zero, so $H^n(c)$ is an isomorphism for every $n$. Hence $c$ is a quasi-isomorphism in either trivial case.

source.place: Tag 0117 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain); exactness with zero kernel cohomology

proof.text: The combinatorial model structure is already supplied by [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model]. Apply that same statement with $R=\mathbf Z$ to identify fibrations and trivial fibrations in abelian-group complexes as degreewise surjections and degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphisms. Steps 1–3 provide its enrichment, tensors and cotensors, while Steps 4–8 verify exactly the Hom comparison axiom in the opening definition of [lem-coef-quillen-section-rectification]. We use only that definition, not the section-rectification conclusion. All lifting in Step 5 is from projective $R$-modules, and no step asserts that such modules are projective over $\mathbf Z$. Thus arbitrary unbounded complexes and rings such as $\mathbf Z/m\mathbf Z$ are included.
